title: Generic normality of flat geometrically reduced families over normal bases
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain and quasi-compact quasi-separated means it has a finite affine open cover whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact. Let $p:Z\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and suppose every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is reduced (all its local rings have no nonzero nilpotents). Then $Z$ is reduced and $\eta$-normal: every finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] $\eta$-modification $Z^{\prime}\to Z$ is an isomorphism. In particular this applies to the curve and marking of every semistable multipointed $S$-curve as defined below. An $\eta$-modification is a proper morphism inducing an isomorphism on the generic fibre and between schematically dense open subschemes; an open $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20--21: flat finitely presented morphisms with reduced geometric fibres over a normal integral base are eta-normal. The semistable and etale instances use the definitions of §1.2.

proof.text: First $Z$ is reduced, and restriction of functions to its generic fibre is injective on every open. Work over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, with $R$ a domain. For an affine open of $Z$ with ring $B$, restriction to the generic fibre is $B\to B\otimes_R\operatorname{Frac}R$. Its kernel consists of elements annihilated by some nonzero $r\in R$. Apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] with the trivial invertible module to exclude these elements. The generic fibre is reduced: its affine rings embed in their tensor product with an algebraic closure of $\operatorname{Frac}R$ (extend a vector-space basis), which is reduced by hypothesis [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Thus a nilpotent of $B$ vanishes. The same affine argument on a cover of any open gives the asserted injectivity.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20–21; agent expansion using the indicated Stacks inputs.

proof.text: Let $f:Z'\to Z$ be any finite $\eta$-modification. Isomorphism of a morphism can be checked on an open cover of its target, so restrict to the inverse images of affine opens of $S$. Apply [lem-trf-normal-approximation-finite-eta-modification] on each such base. It supplies a normal integral Noetherian affine base $S_0$ and the finite $\eta_0$-modification $f_0:Z'_0\to Z_0$ of a flat finitely presented family with reduced geometric fibres. If $f_0$ is an isomorphism, its inverse base changes to an inverse of $f$. Hence it suffices to prove the result on this Noetherian model. In the following steps rename it $(S,Z,Z',f)$; $Z$ and $Z'$ are Noetherian. Here finite presentation implies finite type, and finite morphisms are finite type; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] therefore gives the stated Noetherianity of $Z$ and $Z'$.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20–21; agent expansion using the indicated Stacks inputs.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_{Z'}$. Finiteness says that $f$ is affine and $\mathcal A$ is a finite quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Thus on a Noetherian affine chart the kernel and cokernel of $\mathcal O_Z\to\mathcal A$ are finite modules. Their supports are closed: for a finite module generated by $m_1,\ldots,m_n$, vanishing at a prime means that a single element outside that prime kills all the $m_i$, so it vanishes on a principal neighbourhood. The complement $W$ of these two supports is consequently open, and $f$ is an isomorphism precisely over $W$ by the affine description. The generic fibre lies in $W$: the unit map becomes an isomorphism after generic base localization, and every nonzero base element is already a unit in a stalk lying over the generic point.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20–21; agent expansion using the indicated Stacks inputs.

proof.text: Choose a common schematically dense isomorphism open $V\subset Z$ for $f$. The restriction of $\mathcal A$ to the generic fibre determines its sections: if a section $b$ of $\mathcal A$ vanishes there, then its restriction to $V$ is zero by Step 1, applied to the flat open subscheme $V\subset Z$. Its restriction to $f^{-1}V$ is therefore zero, and schematic density of $f^{-1}V$ in $Z'$ forces $b=0$. Also $\mathcal O_Z\to\mathcal A$ is injective, since its generic-fibre restriction is an isomorphism and Step 1 gives injectivity on $\mathcal O_Z$. Since $W$ contains the generic fibre, these arguments in particular give $\mathcal O_Z\subset\mathcal A\subset j_*\mathcal O_W$, where $j:W\hookrightarrow Z$.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20–21; agent expansion using the indicated Stacks inputs.

proof.text: Let $z$ be a generic point of any fibre. By [lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth] there is a smooth neighbourhood $T$ of $z$. Cover it by affine charts mapping to affine opens of the normal base. The smooth ring-map/affine-smooth equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-normal-ring-normal] show that all local rings of $T$ are integrally closed domains. The base affine rings are normal because normality here means normality at every prime. No smoothness of the entire generic fibre is asserted.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20–21; agent expansion using the indicated Stacks inputs.

proof.text: For an affine open $H\subset T$, a section of $\mathcal A(H)$ restricts to a section on $H\cap V$, integral over $\mathcal O_Z(H)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], since $\mathcal A(H)$ is a finite algebra. The open $H\cap V$ is dense in $H$ by schematic density. Apply [lem-sbc-normal-dense-open-integral-section] on the locally Noetherian normal scheme $T$: the restricted section extends to $\mathcal O_Z(H)$. Schematic density on the source then says that this extension equals the original section of $\mathcal A(H)$. Together with the injection in Step 4 this gives $\mathcal A|_T=\mathcal O_T$. Thus $T\subset W$, and $W$ contains every generic point of every fibre.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20–21; agent expansion using the indicated Stacks inputs.

proof.text: Take $z\notin W$ and $s=p(z)$. Since $W$ contains the generic fibre, $s\ne\eta$. The local domain $R=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ has a nonzero element in its maximal ideal; this element is a nonzerodivisor, so $\operatorname{depth}R\ge1$. The Noetherian local fibre ring $F=\mathcal O_{Z_s,z}$ is reduced (its geometric scalar extension is reduced, and extension of a field is injective on vector spaces). Moreover $z$ is not a fibre-component generic point, so its corresponding prime is not minimal and $\dim F\ge1$. The explicit $(S_1)$ inequality in [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-reduced] gives $\operatorname{depth}F\ge1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] to the flat local map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, whose closed-fibre ring is exactly $F$. It gives $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{Z,z}=\operatorname{depth}R+\operatorname{depth}F\ge2$.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20–21; agent expansion using the indicated Stacks inputs.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-depth-two-hartogs-restriction] with $L=Z$, the open $W$, and $N=\mathcal O_Z$. This is a quasi-coherent module finite on every affine chart, its stalks are finite, $Z$ is locally Noetherian, and Step 7 verifies depth at least two at every point outside $W$. Hence $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_W$ is an isomorphism. The intermediate algebra $\mathcal A$ from Step 4 must therefore equal $\mathcal O_Z$. Finally $f$ is affine with this algebra, so on each affine chart it is $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, and is an isomorphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. This proves $\eta$-normality and, with Step 1, both main conclusions.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20–21; agent expansion using the indicated Stacks inputs.

proof.text: For the semistable curve apply the main conclusion after checking reducedness of every geometric fibre $C$. Such a fibre is locally Noetherian, being locally of finite type over a field. At a permitted singular point its local ring $A$ embeds in its completion: the kernel is $\bigcap_n\mathfrak m^n$, which is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] with $I=\mathfrak m$ and $M=A$. Its completion is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, a reduced ring: evaluation on the two axes embeds it into $\Omega[[u]]\times\Omega[[v]]$, since a series vanishing on both axes has every monomial divisible by $uv$. Each one-variable factor is a domain by taking the lowest nonzero coefficient. Thus $A$ is reduced. At a smooth point choose a smooth open of $C$ and apply [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], which in particular says its local rings are reduced. These two cases cover the fibre, so the curve has reduced geometric fibres.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2, printed pp. 20–21; agent expansion using the indicated Stacks inputs.

proof.text: The marking is etale by semistability, hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Its geometric fibres are reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Both the marking and the curve are flat and finitely presented by the multipointed-curve definition in the statement, so both satisfy the hypotheses of the main conclusion. Empty markings and empty fibres cause no exception.

New node lem-trf-normal-approximation-finite-eta-modification is true: I proved it myself by normalizing finite-type Z-subrings and quotienting Z'_0 by its R_0-torsion to keep schematic density. lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth is true by 056V and 01V9.
